title: Make warnings independent of color
description: Ensure safe-area, provenance, uncalibrated, physical-evidence, partially-used-sheet, offline, and recovery warnings communicate category, consequence, and action through text and semantics rather than color alone.
acceptanceCriteria: Every named warning includes persistent descriptive text and a semantic label or icon with accessible name
Removing color from the interface does not remove warning category, consequence, or corrective action
Demo and physical-evidence-blocked states remain distinguishable in list, detail, preview, and recovery contexts
Warning controls retain visible focus and meet the established contrast treatment

steps.details: Locate the seven named warning classes across editor, preparation, calibration, sheet, offline, import, and recovery states.
Give each variant a stable text label, consequence, corrective action, and optional decorative or accessible icon policy.
Render warnings consistently in compact and detailed contexts without replacing domain-specific reason text.
Assert text/role/name presence for each variant and inspect forced-colors or color-disabled states for understandable focus and warnings.

technicalNotes: Maximum execution scope is ten minutes; standardize the named warning variants and focused checks only.
Icons supplement text and must not be the sole carrier of meaning.
